description_en: The sataḥ was built in 1883 by a Satyal family and features unique and high-quality woodwork including an unusually shaped five-bay window on the first floor and oval windows on the ground floor. The nearby Purohitaghāṭa is the funeral place of the royal priests (Pruscha1975, p 94). The sataḥ was badly damaged during the 2015 earthquakes and was consequently rebuilt under a project financed by the Asia Development Bank (ADB).The building's roof and its first floor collapsed completely in the 2015 earthquakes. The small room in the upper floor of the house takes the form of a shrine and a statue of Viṣṇu was once enshrined here. Nowadays, the statue is kept in the sanctum of the Viṣṇu Temple located behind the sataḥ. As of October 2019, it is temporarily covered with corrugated metal sheets and rescued timber components that were stored in an adjacentsataḥ. The rear courtyard contains four small dome-shaped Śaiva and Vaiṣṇava temples, whilst two stone pillars stand in front of the Sataḥ. Statues of Garuḍa and Hanumān once sat atop these pillars facing one another. However, the Garuḍa statue has gone missing, leaving Hanumān sitting alone.The Sataḥ was built in 1883 by a Satyal family who were residents of Kathmandu (Gutschow2011, 916). A priest from the Giri caste performed its daily ritual worships. On Friday afternoons, people chantbhajanasat thephalcāof the Sataḥ. Hindu monks travelling from India stay here for some days during the Dassain (Daśaĩ) and Śivarātri festivals. On the day of Śrīpañcamī, the present generation of the Satyal family (i.e. the descendants of the founder of the Sataḥ) come here to perform a specialpūjā.Thapa(2014) quotes from Gutschow's Architecture of the Newars: "The sattal at Purohitghat by the Bagmati river is located on a long stretch of stepped embankment that did not start to be architecturally articulated before the 1790s. The sattal at Purohitghat was one of the smaller endowments, but probably the most fascinating one. The baluster columns and the cusped arches of the arcade follow early 19th- century prototypes, but the first floor windows went beyond the scope of carved window frames. The notion of a lintel as a bearing element can only be recognized on the central rectangular opening. The semicircular arches are for the first time not incorporated by a bearing frame but are bearing members themselves. The frames of the side openings add to the stunning design, contributing to a move that culminates in the flower motifs that crown the central opening. In a playful manner, curled appendages frame the entire window, flush with the wall."In 2014, a large debate on whether street art endangers cultural heritage was sparked amongst artists and intellectuals in Kathmandu when the French-Canadian artist Seb Toussaint included the front of the site with his 'Outsiders Krew' in a project entitled 'Share the Word'.
description_ne: टेकु स्थित वाग्मती र विष्णुमतीको दोभानदेखि थापाथलीको कालमोचनसम्मको वाग्मतीकिनारमा शाहकाल र राणाकालमा बनेका धेरैवटा मठ-मन्दिर एवं सतःहरू रहेका छन्। तीमध्ये पुरोहितघाट स्थित सतः पनि एक हो । पचलिघाटबाट करिब ४०० मिटर पूर्वतिर पुरोहितघाट अवस्थित छ । राजपुरोहित खलकको अन्तिम संस्कार गरिने घाट भएकाले यस घाटलाई पुरोहितघाट भनिएको हो (Pruscha1975, 94)। दक्षिणाभिमुख सतः दुईतले थियो । सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पमा माथिल्लो तला भत्केपछि हाल सतःको भुइँतला मात्र बचेको छ । सतःको पिँढीमा भएका पाँच कवलमध्ये बीचको कवलमा सतःको पछाडिको चोकमा प्रवेश गर्ने मुख्य ढोका रहेको छ । सतःको पछाडिको चोकमा चारवटा स-साना गुम्बज शैलीमा बनेका शैव तथा वैष्णव मन्दिरहरू रहेका छन् । सतःको माथिल्लो तलामा भएको सानो कोठालाई देवस्थानको रूप दिई विष्णुको मूर्ति राखिएको थियो । भूकम्पले माथिल्लो तला भत्किएपछि सतः पछाडि भएको विष्णु मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा उक्त मूर्ति सुरक्षित राखिएको छ । सतःको माथिल्लो तलाको मोहोडा भागमा रहेको झ्याल निकै कलात्मक थियो । पाँचवटा झ्यालको एउटै समूह बनाई जडान गरिएको उक्त झ्याल नेपालको परम्परागत शैलीभन्दा पृथक प्रकारको छ । गुत्सो (2011, 919) ले यस झ्यालको काष्ठकलालाई १९ औँ सदीको हाइब्रिड शैली मानेका छन् । सतःको ठिक अगाडि दुईवटा प्रस्तरका स्तम्भहरू खडा छन् । ती स्तम्भमध्ये एकमा हनुमान मूर्ति रहेको छ भने अर्कोमा पहिला गरुडको मूर्ति थियो, अहिले चोरी भैसक्यो ।यो सतःको निर्माण सन् १८८३ मा काठमाडौँ निवासी एक सत्याल परिवाबाट भएको थियो (Gutschow2011, 916)। सतःमा भएको विष्णुमूर्तिमा गिरी थरका व्यक्तिले नित्यपूजा गर्दै आएका छन् । सतःको पिँढीमा प्रत्येक हप्ताको शुक्रबार दिउँसो भजनगायन हुन्छ । शिवरात्रि र दशैँको नौरथामा भारतबाट आएका साधुहरू यस सतःमा केही दिन यहाँ वास बस्ने गर्दछन् । सतःको निर्माता सत्याल परिवारका वर्तमान पुस्ताले विवाहपञ्चमीका दिन यस सतःमा आएर विशेष पूजाआजा गर्दछन् ।

historical_events.event_description: The facade of the Sataḥ was spray-painted by Seb Toussaint, an Anglo-French artist. The monument caught the attention of artists and cultural actors and caused an agitated public debate surrounding the definition of ownership of endangered cultural heritage. Seb Toussaint and his Outsiders Krew were accused of abusing religious sites and local people for the ‘wrong’ purposes; i.e. harming sites through sacrilege and 'insulting' their 'authentic' purposes instead of working to beautify underprivileged sites. The art group travels around the world and visits impoverished and neglected urban settlements, where they invite local inhabitants to ‘participate’ in the beautification of their area by selecting meaningful words that the artists then, sometimes with the help of local artists or laymen, paint on the walls of residential houses. The Sataḥ at Purohitaghāṭa was the first example of a religious compound being used in the art project, which is why it enraged some groups even a few weeks after the wall had been already painted and sprayed. The question of ‘Whose heritage’ was raised, and ranged between accusations of iconoclasm against a Hindu temple (though the Shiva temple lied behind the Sataḥ at Purohitaghāṭa) to damaging heritage structures (such as spraying unremovable paint onto a rare window design from 1883). One critic argued that, “the Shiva Temple, though not on the World Heritage Site List, has something to contribute to the remarkable cultural heritage and legacy of Nepal. Any kind of intruding and defacing it would be overlooking history of the place and hurting sentiments of my people.” (inThapa 2014)The case is also interesting because it draws attention to the fact that the Satah had long been in a dilapidated state and sidelined by public attention. Some Nepalis questioned why this had been the case for so long, and why it took foreign artwork to notice this. As such, these voices found the accusations ambivalent, claiming that had the site been recognised as heritage, people would have cared about its neglected state beforehand. The fact that it was left uncared for for so long was seen as a sign of ignorance on behalf of the Nepalese people vis-à-vis their own heritage.Thapa (2014)refers to Niels Gutschow’s mention of the site in his third volume of Architecture of Newars: “The sattal at Purohitghat was one of the smaller endowments, but probably the most fascinating one. The baluster columns and the cusped arches of the arcade follow early 19th century prototypes, but the first floor windows went beyond the scope of carved window frames … The frames of the side openings add to the stunning design, contributing to a move that culminates in the flower motifs that crown the central opening. In a playful manner, curled appendages frame the entire window, flush with the wall“ (see primary image).Mahaju (2015)connects cultural heritage to the idea of national progress and development for which it has often been sacrificed, showing that cultural heritage has been dramatically endangered in times of urban transformation: “in 1993/4, during the construction of the Bagmati Bridge in Thapathali, the government tore down a historic temple and a pati. What remains of the complex is cramped away in one corner. The government had assured the public that those structures will be relocated with due honour as it merits a place of worship. Twenty one years hence, the promise still hangs in the air. The recent road widening also has upset conservationists and heritage practitioners, common people notwithstanding, at how the government has treated places of utmost importance.”

historical_events.event_name: Collapse of the roof and upper floor
historical_events.event_description: The roof and upper floor of the Sataḥ collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes.
The Sataḥ was constructed by a Satyāla family from Kathmandu.

historical_events.event_name: Theft of Hanumān and Garuḍa statues
historical_events.event_description: The statues of Hanumān and Garuḍa were stolen. Some days later, the statue of Hanumān was found on the banks of the Bagmati close to Kālamocana.

The ruins of the upper floor were left uncovered for about a month after the earthquake. It took about a week for the French Army rescue team of seventy members to remove the ruins. During the removal of the debris, the windows of the Sataḥ were safely collected by the Department of Archaeology in the presence of the local residents.
